# Child Activation Functions

A callable function library for preparing child documents with independently declared parties and explicit identity mappings. It also retains legacy construction using parent role names and inherits activation, party management, access and amendment helpers. Preparing a child returns a modified document; it does not initialize it, obtain consent or establish that it is active.

Document reads refer to the document executing the function, including a nested instruction’s own document. In child preparation, this is the configuring parent; paths modified inside `child` belong to the returned child.

## Explicit child preparation

`prepareChild(child, mapping, suppliedRoles)` requires an uninitialized child: any existing `/contracts/initialized` rejects with `CHILD_ALREADY_INITIALIZED`. Its `/clauses/activation/type` must be the exact Activation Clause type, otherwise `CHILD_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED`.

Party declarations come from the child’s `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`; source parties come from the executing document’s `/activation/parties`.

- `mapping` maps child role names to either parent role names or explicit Party values. Parent parties and child declarations must be nonempty objects; `mapping` must be an object.
- Every declared child role needs a mapping unless listed in `suppliedRoles`, which defaults to `[]`. A supplied role retains its declaration and cannot also be mapped. Unknown mapping keys or supplied slots reject.
- Child role names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Selected values must be Parties and are validated against the child declaration through specialization.
- Each selected Party needs `lead/channel` and a nonempty, duplicate-free `readerKeys` list of nonempty strings. Every parent party’s main identity must appear in the resolved child roster: the same lead channel and the same reader-key set, regardless of key order. Matching business descriptions or role names alone is insufficient.

`bindChild(child, mapping)` calls `prepareChild` with no supplied slots, so every child role requires an explicit mapping.

Preparation replaces the child’s declared `parties` with the resolved roster while preserving its other activation parameters. Existing child `accessPaths` default to `[]`. Each parent `/activation/accessPaths` entry is copied by reference to `/timelineAccess/configurerN`, where `N` is the current child access-path count, and appended to the child’s activation `accessPaths`. An occupied target rejects with `CHILD_ACCESS_PATH_CONFLICT`; absent parent access paths contribute none.

For resolved parties with `lead/channel`, preparation installs lead transports at `/contracts/<role>` and additional representative transports at `/contracts/<role>__<repId>`. An identical existing transport is accepted; a different existing value rejects with `CHILD_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. Supplied slots without a lead channel remain declarations and receive no transports at this stage.

## Legacy construction

`activateChild(child, frozen, readerNames, roles)` returns `child` unchanged when the executing document has no `/activation`. Otherwise, `roles` defaults to `[]`, meaning all parent parties; `readerNames` defaults to `[]`, meaning no additional named reader groups. Selected parties and readers retain their parent names. Missing selections reject with `CHILD_PARTY_NOT_IN_PARENT` or `CHILD_READER_NOT_IN_PARENT`.

This function rebuilds child `timelineAccess` using `grant0`, `grant1`, and subsequent references from parent access paths. It replaces `/clauses/activation` with an Activation Clause, preserving existing parameters except for `parties`, `readers`, `accessPaths`, `frozen` and `required`. `required` retains the child’s existing value or defaults to `[]`; the Boolean `frozen` argument has no defined default. Lead and representative transports are written into child contracts.

Unlike explicit preparation, this legacy function does not check child initialization, require an existing Activation Clause, or reject conflicting transport entries. Its reconstruction can replace existing child access and channel configuration.

## Inherited activation and access

`readerGroups` combines named `readers`, party `readerKeys` and representative `readerKeys`; generated party and representative names overwrite matching named groups. `transports` uses role names for leads and `<role>__<repId>` for additional representatives.

`accessValid` exempts External Channel transports. Other transports must be Timeline Channels. Each must have a matching Timeline Access document at an `accessPaths` location, with the same timeline and provider and at least one allowed key from every reader group in that single access document. An empty reader group cannot satisfy that check. Reading access and operation authority are separate.

`computeState` derives `/activation` readiness from access, approvals for all `required` roles, current negotiated fields and `closed`. Revision-matching pending additions also participate in its access check. `accessReady` and `functional` express access validity; `termsAccepted` expresses required approvals plus current terms; `active` additionally requires that the document is not closed. `status` distinguishes `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`, `ACTIVE` and `CLOSED`; `everActivated` records prior activation. Missing persisted values do not independently establish these outcomes.

`refresh` initializes terms if absent, commits derived state and refreshes access-request readiness. Terms separate the initial definition from configured scalar `negotiation/allowedPaths`, excluding access references, named readers and party reader keys from the definition identity. Missing or nonscalar negotiated fields reject. Initial channels remain empty Composite External Channels until access is ready. State transitions can emit Document Activated, Document Access Suspended or Document Access Restored.

`approve` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion=true`, a party-lead `call/channel`, the current `revision` and valid participant access. With negotiated paths, `termsRef` is required; any supplied reference must match `/activation/terms/ref`. A repeated approval returns successfully without a new acceptance event. A new approval records `approved`, commits state and emits Terms Accepted; it need not activate the document. Activation freezes negotiation editing and supersedes a pending proposal.

`updateParty` also requires exact review and a party-lead channel. `party` defaults to the invoking role; an existing different party cannot be managed. `frozen` blocks changes, and additions require `allowNewParties`. `replacement` needs a lead channel, valid representative names and valid access. Success updates contracts, clears approvals, increments `revision`, adds a new role to `required` when applicable and emits Party Changed. `updatePartyPublic` delegates without requiring an input revision.

`admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, configured admission approvers, valid identities and participant access. Existing roles must retain their main identity; an unchanged roster returns `duplicate`. New admission updates contracts and revision and emits Party Changed. Party or required-role changes update established terms and invalidate pending negotiation; approvals reset when negotiated paths are configured.

Access-installation helpers validate 1–16 native Timeline Access histories, deduplicate by original document identity and register refresh handlers. `requestPartyAddition` ignores stale revisions and repeated `admissionRef` values, validates supplied access documents and may emit Party Access Update Requested. Such a request is neither a permission grant nor confirmation that access changed; permission updates remain provider-owned.

Inherited amendment helpers record proposals against configured paths, revision and editability, then apply a replacement only after every configured approver has approved. Duplicate submissions can return `duplicate`; conflicting, reused or changed proposal identifiers reject. Recording a proposal or one approval does not establish application.

The supplied evidence does not define the Activation Clause’s initialization hooks or negotiation wiring. Callable helpers alone establish neither automatic execution nor a viewer’s permission.
